before.details: Indra closes the Sankaṣṭa glory, saying it became known in the mortal world through Kṛtavīrya’s son and was experienced by gods and kings such as Candraseṇa. Remembrance alone gives accomplishment. Briefly, Rāvaṇa received the printed akhilājñatā and the Pāṇḍavas obtained their kingdom through its favour. Indra says his stalled vimāna will move to Amarāvatī if this vow’s merit is given into his hand. Brahmā says Śūrasena hears joyfully, bows to Indra, praises his own earlier merit for hearing such a vow and begins practicing. No merit transfer or actual departure occurs here.
before.outcome: The exemplum returns to the stalled-vimāna frame with a conditional merit request; Śūrasena starts a vow, while the vehicle remains unresolved.

before.details: Royal messengers recount their mission: Indra rode to see Gṛtsamāda, came to Bhṛśuṇḍi with gods, bowed and worshipped, received permission and worship, and headed home. In Śūrasena’s city his vehicle fell through the gaze of a leprous Vaiśya son. Indra told the king that Sankaṣṭa merit would restart it, prompting the search. They propose taking this woman to the king so she can transfer vow merit, afterward gain twice the merit and resume her ascent while Indra’s vehicle returns home. Gaṇeśa’s servants refuse, saying they have no order from him to give her to someone else.
before.outcome: Merit transfer and doubling are only a royal-emissary proposal; divine messengers refuse without Gaṇeśa’s authorization.

before.details: The servants place her on the vimāna; she immediately gains divine radiance, clothing and ornaments and is taken toward Gaṇeśa amid divine music. before.details: The messengers immediately put all the city’s beings aboard, explicitly all caturākaraja creatures, with divine clothes and ornaments. Some wonder how they gained this without their own merit; others attribute rescue to the king’s merit, comparing metal becoming gold through a treasure and sinners attaining perfection through saintly speech. The attendants attempt upward movement, but the craft remains inert on earth. Some spot a leprous man and urge discarding him, saying the craft will rise when he descends. Śūrasena instead offers to exclude himself and carry all others, or asks the man’s former birth, sin and a compassionate remedy. The messengers reassure him and undertake to explain. Numbering prints15 at position35 and4 at41.
before.outcome: All classes are accommodated, but lift actually fails. The king refuses the proposed abandonment and explicitly seeks remedy or his own exclusion.

before.details: After much time Budha visits sage Kalabha’s house while the sage bathes, seizes his beautiful wife by the hair, embraces, kisses and rapes her. Sulabhā says her parents’ given name has made her easy to him, condemns the assault in her husband’s absence and curses him to become a leper in another birth whose very name people will avoid. He flees frightened to the prostitute but resumes drink and pleasure. Brahmā declines further wrongdoings, saying telling others’ faults diminishes merit. Budha eventually dies; Yama orders messengers to throw him into hell until the elemental dissolution. Having endured that, he is born in a Vaiśya home, severely leprous through the sage’s wife’s curse. The discourse condemns his deeds, prescribes clothed bathing after touching him and avoidance of his name, and says removing him will raise the craft.
before.outcome: The curse specifies a later birth; actual hell and Vaiśya-leper rebirth are narrated, ending the past-life explanation before the king requests mercy.

before.details: Hearing the messengers’ account, Śūrasena trembles, says he did not know these acts, rises and bows anxiously. He asks compassionately for a way to remove all the wrongdoer’s defects. They tell him to rise and listen: Gaṇeśa has a famous FOUR-syllable name; japa it into the man’s ear and all faults will cease like darkness at sunrise. They say he is not qualified for other remedies, so the name alone should be japped.
before.outcome: The king seeks restoration, and the servants prescribe an auditory name remedy with an explicit limitation.

before.details: Having heard and seen the vow’s greatness, Śūrasena asks Vasiṣṭha for a suitable time to practice a vow giving immediate assurance. The sage prescribes Māgha dark fourth on Tuesday.
